We will use participation, feedback, outcomes and delivery learning to strengthen the model before expanding across wider Norfolk.

homeOffer.heading: Practical support around maternity care
homeOffer.body: GNI helps women and families understand maternity services, prepare for birth and early parenthood, build confidence in decision-making, and connect with appropriate clinical and community support. GNI complements NHS maternity care; it does not replace a midwife, GP, obstetric team, maternity triage or emergency service.

about.introDesc: Go Nurture Initiative CIC is an independent, asset-locked Community Interest Company established to improve access to culturally responsive, trauma-informed perinatal education and community support. We begin in Norwich, with an evidence-led plan to expand across wider Norfolk and, when the model is ready, beyond the county.
about.missionDesc: Every woman should be able to understand her maternity care, participate meaningfully in decisions and access trustworthy support, regardless of ethnicity, language, migration experience, income or familiarity with UK services. GNI helps bridge the gap between clinical maternity care and the additional education, navigation and community connection that some women and families need.
about.pilotTitle: 30 women. Three antenatal cohorts. Weekly infant-feeding clinics.
about.pilotDesc: Our Year 1 plan is to support up to 30 women through three six-week antenatal cohorts of The Favour Oloye Birth Confidence Programme (FOBCP). Partners and supporters may participate as appropriate, while additional eligible women may access infant-feeding clinics through direct referral. We will evaluate reach, experience, outcomes, accessibility, safety and cost before wider expansion.
about.referralDesc: Referral partners may include community midwives, GP practices, maternity services, health visitors, local authority teams, voluntary and community organisations, refugee and migrant support organisations, and trusted faith and community groups. Acceptance remains subject to eligibility, consent, safeguarding considerations and available capacity.
about.valuesIntro: Faith, Growth and Relationships guide GNI’s governance, partnerships and delivery.
about.faithBody: We respect the faith, beliefs, cultures and spiritual identities of the people we serve. We may work with churches, mosques, temples and other trusted community groups, while welcoming participants of every faith and none. GNI does not impose religious belief or practice.
about.growthBody: We learn from participants, evidence, partners and evaluation. We use that learning to improve quality, accessibility and the responsible development of our services.
about.relationshipsBody: We build trusted relationships around women and families while maintaining clear professional boundaries. We work with maternity services, primary care, local authorities, voluntary organisations, faith groups and community networks to strengthen referral and support pathways.
about.licenceTitle: Created by Favour Oloye, delivered with care
about.licenceDesc: The Favour Oloye Birth Confidence Programme was created and is personally owned by Favour Oloye. GNI delivers the programme under a written royalty-free community licence. This arrangement protects the programme’s intellectual property while allowing GNI to provide the community service without paying a commercial licence fee.
about.independenceDesc: GNI is legally and operationally separate from Nurtured & Nourished Women’s Health Ltd. Any future collaboration, sponsorship, licence or service agreement between the organisations will be documented transparently, managed through GNI’s conflicts-of-interest process and considered in the best interests of GNI and its beneficiaries.
about.teamQuote: We are women, clinicians and community members. We built this with our communities, for our communities.
about.member1Bio: Registered Nurse, Antenatal Educator and trainee Lactation Consultant. Favour founded GNI from her professional knowledge, community insight and lived experience of navigating maternity and infant feeding in the UK. She leads programme development, partnerships and delivery.
about.member2Bio: Marion is a Certified Lactation Specialist, Breastfeeding Counsellor and Mindful Breastfeeding Practitioner, and Director of Breastfeeding Support Norwich & Norfolk. She offers warm, evidence-based breastfeeding and lactation support to families across Norwich and Norfolk, whether that's working through a tricky latch, navigating pumping, or just having someone to sit with you and listen without judgement. She's passionate about supporting families and committed to inclusive, culturally sensitive care, and she is honoured to support Black mothers as part of this community.
about.member3Bio: A qualified accountant who contributes financial oversight, governance and sustainability expertise.
about.member4Bio: A cybersecurity professional who contributes data-protection, digital-safety and systems expertise.
about.member5Bio: Registered Nurse and Registered Midwife. Abimbola is deeply passionate about maternal health and advocating for women from BAME and Displaced backgrounds. She brings clinical expertise and a warm, culturally aware approach to our perinatal education, helping women feel seen, heard, and supported.
about.member6Bio: Registered Nurse with a heart for community health. Grace is passionate about breaking down barriers to care for women in our target communities. She supports the delivery of our free education and feeding support, ensuring every woman receives practical help with dignity and respect.

programmes.introTitleHighlight: for pregnancy, birth and early parenthood
programmes.introDesc: Our services are free and referral-led. They are designed for Black, Asian and other minoritised ethnic women, displaced women, and women facing barriers to understanding or accessing maternity information and support in Norwich.
programmes.cohortsLabel: THE FAVOUR OLOYE BIRTH CONFIDENCE PROGRAMME (FOBCP)
programmes.cohortsTitle: Six weeks of practical, partner-inclusive antenatal education
programmes.cohortsDesc: FOBCP is a six-week antenatal course with a separately scheduled postnatal reunion. It helps participants understand pregnancy, labour, birth, infant feeding, early parenthood, recovery, emotional wellbeing and the UK maternity system. The programme brings together four pillars—Body, Soul, Spirit and Village—and uses the VOICE framework to support informed conversations and decisions. Partners or chosen supporters are included throughout.
programmes.fobcpNote: FOBCP was created and is personally owned by Favour Oloye. GNI delivers it under a royalty-free community licence.
programmes.feedingClinicDesc: Our planned weekly clinics provide a welcoming space to discuss breastfeeding, expressing, responsive feeding and common early feeding concerns. Women may be referred from an FOBCP cohort or directly through an eligible referral partner. Support is provided within the competence and capacity of the clinic team, with referral to NHS or specialist services when concerns fall outside GNI’s scope.
programmes.postnatalReunionTitle: Reflect, reconnect and find the right next support
programmes.postnatalReunionDesc: Participants are invited to a postnatal reunion after their antenatal course. The reunion provides an opportunity to reflect on birth and early parenthood, reconnect with the group, identify further support needs and receive appropriate signposting. It is not a substitute for postnatal clinical care.
programmes.languageAccessDesc: We ask about language, communication, literacy, disability, cultural and practical access needs during referral and enrolment. Interpretation, translated information and reasonable adjustments are arranged according to assessed need, availability and funding. Participants or referrers should tell us as early as possible what support is required.
programmes.partnersDesc: Referral partners may include community midwives, GP practices, maternity services, health visitors, local authority teams, refugee and migrant support organisations, voluntary and community organisations, and trusted faith and community groups. A referral does not replace clinical assessment and does not guarantee a place where eligibility or capacity requirements are not met.

communitySupport.introDesc: GNI works with maternity and primary-care professionals, local authorities, voluntary organisations, migrant and refugee services, and trusted faith and community groups. Together, we help eligible women find appropriate education, feeding support and wider services without duplicating NHS clinical care.
communitySupport.partnersTitle: Partners who already know and support women locally
communitySupport.partnersDesc: Our referral network may include community midwives, GP practices, NHS maternity teams, health visitors, local authority services, voluntary and community organisations, refugee and migrant support organisations, churches, mosques, temples and other trusted community groups. Each partner remains responsible for working within its own role, competence and safeguarding duties.
communitySupport.supportDesc1: Referral-led antenatal education and birth preparation through FOBCP
communitySupport.supportDesc3: Help to understand and navigate UK maternity services
communitySupport.supportDesc5: Interpretation and accessible formats according to assessed need, availability and funding
communitySupport.supportDesc6: Community connection, signposting and referral to appropriate services
communitySupport.boundaryStatement: GNI does not provide emergency, diagnostic or routine maternity care. Urgent or clinical concerns should be directed to the participant’s midwife, maternity triage, GP, NHS 111 or 999, according to the situation.
communitySupport.involveDesc: If your organisation supports eligible women in Norwich and would like to discuss referrals, accessibility or partnership working, please contact us. We will explain the referral criteria, consent requirements, safeguarding arrangements, service boundaries and current capacity before referrals begin.

contact.introTitle: We would be pleased to hear
contact.introDesc: Contact us if you are interested in referrals, partnership, funding, volunteering or learning more about our Norwich programmes. Please do not use this website for urgent medical concerns or emergencies.
contact.partnerDesc: Healthcare professionals, GP practices, community midwives, maternity services, local-authority teams, voluntary organisations and trusted community or faith groups may also contact us here to discuss becoming referral partners. Please do not include detailed medical information in this general contact form.

contact.safetyMessage: GNI is not an emergency or clinical advice service. For urgent maternity concerns, contact your maternity triage service or another clinical service named in your maternity notes. Contact NHS 111 when urgent advice is needed and the situation is not life-threatening. Call 999 in an emergency.
